explanations.explanation: Violence is it. The earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence (Genesis 6:11). Then verse 12 says all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways. That's not one corner of the earth, friend. That's the whole neighborhood.

Famine is a real thing in the Bible, like in Ruth 1:1, but it's not in this verse. Here the earth is corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence. Verse 12 says all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways. Nothing in these verses says the food ran out.

Idols cause trouble in other parts of the Bible, but they're not named in this verse. Verse 11 says the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence. Verse 12 adds that all living creatures had corrupted their ways. So the word that fits is violence.

Easy one to slip past, since the first half of the verse talks about the creatures. But keep reading, because God says, “Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.” Both, friend. The earth is in that sentence too, so the answer is False.

False is right, and the word that settles it is “both.” God says, “Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.” That's the creatures and the earth together, in one sentence. It's a tiny word doing heavy lifting, friend.

An ark. God says, “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.” That's a vessel with rooms, coated inside and out. The biggest thing I ever built was a tower of cookie boxes, and it fell over. Noah got a lot more instructions than I ever did.

An altar is a place for offerings, and this verse doesn't mention one. God says, “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood…” That's a build with rooms and pitch inside and out. I'll give you this much: altar and ark both start with A, so I see how it happened.

No tower in this verse, friend. God tells Noah to make an ark of gopher wood, with rooms inside and pitch inside and out. A tower and an ark are both big building jobs, so I see why it crossed your mind. This plan has rooms, a door in the side and three decks (Genesis 6:16).

Floodwaters. God says, “And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life.” I think that's why the plan is an ark and not a really big oven. Everything on the earth will perish, He says. Heavy words, but notice He tells Noah ahead of time.

Fire is a fair guess for a guy who lives next to ovens all day. But verse 17 says floodwaters. Water, not flames. God says He will bring them “…to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life.” So the answer is floodwaters.

I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so darkness and I go way back. But that's not what God names here. Verse 17 says He will bring floodwaters upon the earth. Water is what He names, friend, not the lights going out.

His covenant. God says, “But I will establish My covenant with you…” A covenant is a binding promise, and it lands right after all that talk of floodwaters. Noah hears the hard news and a promise in the same speech. I think that's worth noticing, friend.

God's kingdom is a big theme in the Bible, but it isn't in this verse. God says, “But I will establish My covenant with you…” A covenant is a binding promise made to Noah. So the word to hold onto is covenant, friend.

No priesthood here, friend. God says, “But I will establish My covenant with you…” That is a binding promise, and it comes right after the floodwaters are announced. Priesthood sounds official, I'll give you that, but covenant is the word.

explanations.answer: His wife and sons and their wives
explanations.explanation: His wife, his sons and their wives. God says, “…you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.” So Noah isn't walking in alone. His whole household is coming along. I think Noah was glad not to go in by himself.

explanations.answer: His father Lamech and his brothers
explanations.explanation: Lamech, Noah's father (Genesis 5:28-29), isn't on the list. God names Noah, his sons, his wife and his sons' wives. The line says, “…you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.” No brothers are mentioned here either.

explanations.answer: His sons and all their servants
explanations.explanation: No servants in this verse, friend. God lists, “…you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.” That's Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives. Nobody else is named in that line.

True. God says, “Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.” They come to Noah. I think that's a relief for a man who already has a giant ark to build. If I had to chase down every creature, I'd still be out there with a net.

This one is actually true. In verse 20 God says, “Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.” Every kind, friend, and they come to Noah. It's a big line, so I get why it's easy to doubt.

Everything, and precisely at that. “So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.” I follow a recipe most of the way, and then I get creative. Noah doesn't get creative, he gets it done. That's a whole lot of instructions to carry out.

explanations.answer: Most of it with a few changes
explanations.explanation: Not a few changes. Verse 22 says, “So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.” Everything, and precisely. No edits are mentioned. I'd have been tempted to tweak a few things, I promise you.

explanations.answer: Just the ark and nothing more
explanations.explanation: The ark is a big part, but the verse says more than that. “So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.” God also gave the animal list and the food list, and the verse says everything. The text doesn't stop at the ark, friend.

He found Noah righteous. The LORD says, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.” That's the reason, right there in the speech. It's the same Noah we met earlier as righteous and blameless (Genesis 6:9). Short and clear, like a recipe card I wish I'd had.

Nothing in the text about finishing early. The LORD gives His reason: “…because I have found you righteous in this generation.” That's about who Noah is, not how fast he built. I wouldn't win a speed prize for building anything either.

Noah makes no promise in this verse. The LORD's reason is “…because I have found you righteous in this generation.” That's what He says to Noah, plain and simple. Half my promises start with 'I'll bake them tomorrow,' and we all know how that goes.

Offspring. God wants seven pairs of birds on the ark “to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.” Offspring means the young ones that come after. The text says that's what the pairs are there to preserve.

Names don't come up in this verse. God says the seven pairs are there “to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.” Offspring means the young ones that come after. I doubt Noah had time for name tags, friend.

Land is close, because the end of the verse says earth. The full phrase is “to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.” So the missing word is offspring, the young ones that come after. Easy to mix up when earth is sitting right there.

Forty. God says He will send rain on the earth “…for forty days and forty nights.” Verse 12 says the rain fell that long. My longest bake is under an hour, and I still hover by the oven like a worried neighbor.
Twenty is short by half. Verse 4 says rain “for forty days and forty nights,” and verse 12 says the rain fell that long. Forty, friend. Twenty days would have been a much shorter story.
Thirty is closer, but it's ten days short. God says in verse 4 that He will send rain “for forty days and forty nights.” Verse 12 says the rain fell that long. So forty is the number.

Not quite. Verse 8 lists “The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground” as coming to Noah. So the unclean animals come too, along with the birds and the crawlers. The text says clean and unclean both, friend.
False is right. Verse 8 lists “The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground” as coming to Noah. Clean and unclean both come. It's not a clean-only guest list.

True. God said seven days from now in verse 4, and verse 10 says, “And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.” Same number, same result. Seven days to finish packing, friend. I'd have used all seven and still forgotten something.
This one is actually true. Verse 10 says, “And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.” That matches what God told Noah in verse 4. Seven days, just as He said.

explanations.answer: The great deep and the heavens
explanations.explanation: The great deep and the heavens. Verse 11 says, “…all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.” That's water from below and water from above at once. I think there was no dry corner anywhere.

explanations.answer: The rivers flowing out of Eden
explanations.explanation: Rivers out of Eden is a thoughtful guess, since a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden (Genesis 2:10). But this verse names a different source. It says, “…all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.” Water from below and from above.

explanations.answer: The Jordan and the Salt Sea
explanations.explanation: The Jordan and the Salt Sea aren't named in this passage. Verse 11 says, “…all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.” So the water comes from the great deep and the heavens. Those sound bigger than any one river, I think.
The LORD. Verse 16 says, “Then the LORD shut him in.” Noah goes in as God commanded, and the LORD is the one who shuts the door. The verse doesn't say how, friend, only who.
Shem, one of Noah's three sons, does go into the ark. But he isn't the one who shuts the door. Verse 16 says, “Then the LORD shut him in.” The shutting belongs to the LORD.
Noah is the one going in, but he isn't the one who shuts the door. Verse 16 says, “Then the LORD shut him in.” The text gives that part to the LORD. Noah just has to walk through, friend.

explanations.answer: It is lifted high above the earth
explanations.explanation: Lifted up. Verse 17 says, “…the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.” Verse 18 adds that the ark floated on the surface of the waters. Nothing about steering is mentioned here, just the ark going up with the water.

explanations.answer: It gets stuck deep in the mud
explanations.explanation: Stuck in the mud is a scary thought, but the text goes the other way. Verse 17 says, “…the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.” Verse 18 says the ark floated on the surface of the waters. Up, not down, friend.

explanations.answer: It is broken apart by the waves
explanations.explanation: Nothing in the text says the waves break the ark apart. Verse 17 says, “…the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.” Verse 18 says it floated on the surface of the waters. The ark rides up with the water, friend.

Over all the high mountains. Verse 19 says, “…all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.” That's no puddle, friend. Verse 20 adds that the waters covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.

explanations.answer: Up to the tops of the trees
explanations.explanation: Tops of the trees is a reasonable guess, but the text goes much higher. Verse 19 says, “…all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.” Trees don't even get mentioned. Mountains, friend.

Halfway up the hills would still leave plenty of dry ground. The text says, “…all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.” Verse 20 adds that the mountaintops were covered to a depth of fifteen cubits. That's far past halfway, friend.

Perished. I'll be gentle here, because this one hurts. Verse 21 says every living thing that moved upon the earth perished, and God had said, “Everything on the earth will perish.” (Genesis 6:17) Birds, livestock, animals and all mankind are named. The text doesn't hurry past it, and neither will I.

Fled is a hopeful word, and I wish the text used it. But verse 21 says every living thing that moved upon the earth perished. This part is heavy, and I'd rather be plain than pretend otherwise. The word is perished.

Hid sounds like a way out, but verse 21 says every living thing that moved upon the earth perished. It names birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms and all mankind. I know that's hard to read, friend. The word is perished.

True. Verse 23 says every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed, and “…only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.” That's a quiet, heavy verse. Notice who remained, though: Noah and those with him, still in the ark.

This one is actually true. Verse 23 says, “…only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.” Everything else on the face of the earth was destroyed. That's a sobering line, friend. The ark's passengers are the ones still here.
